intent.raw_query: Maldives honeymoon for 2, $5000 budget, snorkeling and luxury resorts, March 2026

selected_hotel.name: North Malé Atoll, Maldives Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Private Sunset Dhoni Cruise with Champagne
experiences.description: Sail across the turquoise Indian Ocean on a traditional Maldivian dhoni boat, privately chartered for two. Watch the sun melt into the horizon while sipping champagne and enjoying a curated platter of local and international delicacies. A quintessential romantic experience perfect for honeymooners.

experiences.name: Coral Reef Snorkeling at Banana Reef
experiences.description: Explore one of the Maldives' most iconic and vibrant coral reefs, teeming with parrotfish, moray eels, sea turtles, and colorful reef sharks. Guided snorkeling tours provide equipment and expert narration, making this an unforgettable underwater adventure for couples and luxury travelers alike.

experiences.name: Underwater Spa Treatment for Two
experiences.description: Indulge in a couples' massage or spa ritual in a semi-submerged treatment room surrounded by the ocean. Many luxury resorts offer glass-floor or open-air overwater spa pavilions where you can hear the waves and watch marine life while being pampered with traditional Maldivian coconut and frangipani treatments.

experiences.name: Private Sandbank Picnic Dinner
experiences.description: Be whisked away by speedboat to a secluded, uninhabited sandbank in the middle of the ocean. A personal butler sets up a candlelit dinner table on the white sand, complete with fresh Maldivian seafood, tropical fruits, and fine wine under a canopy of stars — the ultimate honeymoon dining experience.

experiences.name: Maldivian Cooking Class and Local Market Visit
experiences.description: Discover the rich culinary heritage of the Maldives with a hands-on cooking class led by a local chef. Begin with a guided tour of the Malé local market to source fresh tuna, coconut, and tropical spices, then learn to prepare traditional dishes like Mas Huni (tuna and coconut salad) and Garudhiya (fish broth). A culturally immersive and delicious experience.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Maldives
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: North Malé Atoll, Maldives Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Velana International Airport at 13:00. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage. Take a budget-friendly public ferry (around $1–2 USD) from the airport jetty to your guesthouse in North Malé Atoll. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely walk around the local island to get oriented — explore the harbor, local shops, and beachfront.
day_by_day.evening: Watch your first Maldivian sunset from the island beach. Stroll along the shore, take photos, and soak in the atmosphere. Visit a local teashop (sai hotel) for a traditional Maldivian short eats welcome snack.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a quick bite at the airport café (~$5–8 USD)
meals.lunch: Grab a quick meal at a local café near the ferry terminal — try a fish sandwich or short eats (~$3–5 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local restaurant on the island — try Maldivian fish curry with rice (mas riha) (~$5–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some USD to MVR (Maldivian Rufiyaa) at the airport for small local purchases. Public ferries are the most budget-friendly transport option. Confirm ferry schedules in advance as they may be limited in the afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning beach walk and sunrise viewing. After breakfast, rent a snorkel set from your guesthouse or a local shop (~$5–8 USD/day) and head to the nearest house reef for your first snorkeling session. Explore colorful coral gardens and spot tropical fish, sea turtles, and reef sharks in the calm morning waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short local ferry or dhoni boat to a nearby sandbank (~$5–10 USD round trip arranged through guesthouse). Spend the afternoon relaxing on a pristine white sandbank, swimming in turquoise lagoon waters, and enjoying the romance of an isolated sliver of paradise.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the island before sunset. Enjoy a romantic beachside walk as the sky turns golden. Visit the local harbor to watch fishermen return with their catch — a truly authentic Maldivian experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at guesthouse or local café — roshi (flatbread) with coconut chutney and tea (~$3–5 USD)
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic lunch from a local bakery to enjoy on the sandbank (~$4–6 USD)
meals.dinner: Fresh grilled fish dinner at a local restaurant — ask for the catch of the day (~$7–10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Apply reef-safe sunscreen generously before snorkeling. Sandbank visits are best in the morning to early afternoon — afternoon winds can pick up. Negotiate sandbank trips with your guesthouse for better rates.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget group snorkeling excursion organized by your guesthouse (~$20–30 USD per person). Visit two or three different snorkeling spots around North Malé Atoll, including a coral garden and a potential manta ray or shark point. These group tours are significantly cheaper than private charters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the local island's main village area. Explore the island's mosque (dress modestly — cover shoulders and knees), local market, and artisan shops. Pick up affordable Maldivian souvenirs like lacquerware, woven mats, or local spices.
day_by_day.evening: Romantic evening on the beach — lay out a beach mat and stargaze. The Maldives has minimal light pollution on local islands, making for spectacular stargazing. Enjoy a quiet, intimate evening together.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at guesthouse (~$4–6 USD) — eggs, toast, fresh tropical fruit
meals.lunch: Lunch on the snorkeling boat or back at a local eatery — tuna wrap or fish soup (~$4–7 USD)
meals.dinner: Try a local Maldivian home-style restaurant for garudhiya (tuna broth soup) with rice and lime (~$5–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Group snorkeling tours are the best value — ask your guesthouse to connect you with local operators. When visiting mosques and inhabited island areas, women should carry a scarf and men should avoid shorts.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga or meditation on the beach at sunrise — many budget guesthouses offer complimentary or low-cost yoga sessions. Alternatively, enjoy a slow romantic morning with coffee watching the ocean from your room or the guesthouse terrace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a public ferry to Malé city (~$1 USD) — the capital island is just a short ride away. Explore the vibrant capital: visit the iconic Hukuru Miskiy (Old Friday Mosque) built in 1658 from coral stone, the National Museum (entry ~$3 USD), and the colorful local market.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Malé's local fish market at the harbor — an incredible sensory experience as fishermen bring in yellowfin tuna. Browse the night market stalls for affordable street food. Take the last ferry back to your island.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at guesthouse — fresh fruit, yogurt, and tea (~$3–5 USD)
meals.lunch: Lunch in Malé at a local café — try hedhikaa (Maldivian short eats) and tea for an authentic cheap meal (~$3–5 USD)
meals.dinner: Street food dinner at Malé's local eateries before catching the ferry back — fish roshi or tuna curry (~$4–6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry schedules carefully — the last ferry back from Malé may be in the early evening. Keep your valuables secure in the busy capital. The fish market is most active in the late afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise snorkeling session at the house reef — early morning is the best time for calm waters and active marine life. Look for sea turtles feeding on the coral, octopus hiding in crevices, and schools of colorful reef fish.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax and enjoy a slow romantic afternoon. Set up on the beach with a good book, swim in the lagoon, or enjoy the guesthouse's facilities. Many budget guesthouses have rooftop terraces with ocean views — perfect for a lazy honeymoon afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Arrange a budget-friendly private sunset cruise on a traditional Maldivian dhoni boat (~$25–40 USD for a couple, arranged through guesthouse). Enjoy the golden hour on the water with your partner — a romantic highlight of the honeymoon.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast — pancakes with honey and coconut, fresh juice (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the guesthouse or beach café — tuna salad sandwich and coconut water (~$5–7 USD)
meals.dinner: Special romantic dinner at the best local restaurant on the island — order fresh lobster or grilled reef fish if available (~$12–18 USD for two — a splurge but worth it!)

day_by_day.notes: Friday is the Maldivian weekend — some local shops and services may have reduced hours. The sunset dhoni cruise is one of the most romantic budget-friendly experiences available — book at least a day in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Join a dolphin watching excursion — a popular and affordable group tour (~$20–25 USD per person). Head out into the open ocean early morning when spinner dolphins are most active. Watching hundreds of dolphins leap alongside the boat is a magical, unforgettable experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After returning from the dolphin trip, spend the afternoon exploring a different part of your island on foot or by bicycle (rent for ~$3–5 USD/day). Discover hidden beaches, local life, and quiet spots away from the main beach area.
day_by_day.evening: Couples' relaxation evening — many guesthouses offer affordable in-room or garden massage packages (~$20–35 USD per person for a traditional Maldivian massage). Enjoy a soothing massage followed by stargazing on the beach.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at guesthouse before the dolphin trip — eggs, toast, tea (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Late lunch after returning — fresh fish curry at a local eatery (~$5–8 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at guesthouse restaurant or nearby local spot — try mas huni (tuna with coconut) with roshi (~$5–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Dolphin trips are best in the early morning — book the evening before. Bring motion sickness medication if you're prone to seasickness as the open ocean can be choppy. Spinner dolphins are most commonly seen in the Maldives from December to April.

day_by_day.morning: Mid-trip relaxation day. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Spend the morning swimming and snorkeling at your own pace at the house reef. This is a great day to practice underwater photography if you have a waterproof camera or phone case.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short excursion to a nearby uninhabited island (~$10–15 USD arranged through guesthouse). Enjoy complete privacy on a deserted island — swim, sunbathe, collect shells, and enjoy the rare feeling of having a tropical island almost entirely to yourselves.
day_by_day.evening: Return before sunset. Cook or arrange a simple beachside picnic dinner with items from the local shop — fresh fruit, crackers, local snacks, and coconut. A simple but incredibly romantic private beach dinner.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely guesthouse breakfast — French toast with tropical fruit compote (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the uninhabited island — sandwiches, fruit, and coconut water from local shop (~$5–8 USD)
meals.dinner: DIY romantic beach picnic — local cheeses, crackers, tropical fruit, fresh coconut (~$8–12 USD total from local shop)

day_by_day.notes: Uninhabited island trips can often be combined with snorkeling stops — ask your guesthouse operator to include a reef stop on the way. Bring plenty of water and sunscreen as there is no shade or facilities on uninhabited islands.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning fishing trip with local fishermen — traditional Maldivian hand-line fishing (~$15–25 USD per person). This authentic experience gives you insight into local culture and you may catch your own breakfast. Many operators will cook your catch for you.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local island school or community project if your guesthouse can arrange it — a meaningful cultural exchange. Alternatively, take a cooking class to learn how to make traditional Maldivian dishes like mas huni or fish curry (~$20–30 USD per person at some guesthouses).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a beautiful evening walk around the island perimeter as the sun sets. Stop at a local teashop for traditional Maldivian tea and short eats — a beloved local evening ritual and a wonderful way to connect with locals.

meals.breakfast: Freshly caught and grilled fish from the morning fishing trip — the ultimate fresh breakfast (~$0 if included in tour, or $5–8 USD)
meals.lunch: Local café lunch — fish soup (garudhiya) with steamed rice and lime (~$4–6 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at guesthouse — try the local chef's special of the day (~$6–10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The fishing experience is one of the most authentic cultural activities available on a budget. Hand-line fishing (jigging) is the traditional Maldivian method — no rods, just lines. This is a wonderful shared experience for couples.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day snorkeling adventure — arrange a budget group day trip to some of North Malé Atoll's best snorkeling sites (~$30–50 USD per person including lunch). Sites may include Banana Reef, HP Reef, or Manta Point depending on season and operator availability.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the day snorkeling excursion — afternoon sites often include a coral garden and a turtle cleaning station where sea turtles come to have parasites removed by cleaner fish. An extraordinary natural spectacle.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the island tired but exhilarated. Enjoy a quiet, relaxing evening. Write in a travel journal together, review your best underwater photos, and plan the remaining days of your trip.

meals.breakfast: Early guesthouse breakfast before departure — roshi, eggs, tea (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Lunch included on the boat — typically a simple Maldivian meal of rice, curry, and salad
meals.dinner: Relaxed dinner at local restaurant — grilled tuna steak with vegetables and rice (~$7–10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: North Malé Atoll has some of the best snorkeling sites in the Maldives. Banana Reef is one of the most famous dive/snorkel sites in the entire country. Book this excursion a day or two in advance as it's popular. Bring an underwater camera or GoPro for incredible footage.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the full day excursion. Enjoy a slow breakfast and a gentle swim in the lagoon. Take time for a romantic morning coffee on your balcony or the guesthouse terrace watching the ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Malé again for any remaining shopping and sightseeing (~$1 USD ferry). Visit the Maldives Islamic Centre with its golden dome — one of the most photogenic buildings in the capital. Browse the local souvenir market for last-minute gifts — lacquerware, sarongs, and local crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Malé's waterfront promenade (Boduthakurufaanu Magu) in the evening when locals come out to stroll and socialize. Enjoy the lively atmosphere, street food, and harbor views before taking the ferry back.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast — fresh fruit platter, yogurt, granola (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Lunch in Malé — visit a local canteen for a full Maldivian meal of rice, three curries, and salad (~$4–7 USD)
meals.dinner: Back on the island — fresh grilled fish at a beachside local restaurant (~$7–10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Budget souvenir shopping tip: the local market near the harbor in Malé offers much better prices than resort gift shops. Bargaining is not common in the Maldives but you can politely ask for a discount on multiple items.

day_by_day.morning: Final major snorkeling session — return to your favorite reef spot for one last morning of underwater exploration. Take your time and appreciate the incredible marine biodiversity. Try to spot any marine life you may have missed on previous visits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend a leisurely afternoon on the beach — build sandcastles, collect shells, swim, and simply enjoy being in paradise. This is a perfect afternoon for couples to relax and be present together before the trip winds down.
day_by_day.evening: Special honeymoon/romantic celebration dinner — splurge slightly on a nicer meal at the best restaurant available on the island or arrange a special beach dinner setup through your guesthouse (~$30–50 USD total for two — a one-time splurge). Toast to your honeymoon with fresh coconuts or a local drink.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast — eggs benedict or pancakes if available, fresh juice (~$5–7 USD)
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch — fresh coconut, fruit, and a light snack from local shop (~$4–6 USD)
meals.dinner: Special celebration dinner — fresh lobster or premium seafood platter with candles on the beach (~$30–50 USD for two as a special treat)

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the special beach dinner setup at least a day in advance with your guesthouse. Many budget guesthouses can arrange a simple but romantic candlelit beach dinner for couples at a reasonable cost. This is a wonderful way to celebrate your honeymoon.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise viewing together on the beach — wake up early for one last magical Maldivian sunrise. Take plenty of photos and videos to remember the moment. Enjoy a slow, nostalgic morning walk along the beach collecting your last shells.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin packing and organizing your luggage. Do a final snorkel or swim to say goodbye to the reef. Visit any local shops you haven't been to yet for any remaining souvenirs. Return any rented equipment (snorkel gear, bicycle).
day_by_day.evening: Final evening on the island — sit on the beach and watch the last sunset of your trip. Reflect on your honeymoon memories together. Enjoy a relaxed farewell dinner at your favorite local restaurant from the trip.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast — full spread to fuel the last full day (~$5–7 USD)
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at local café — whatever you've enjoyed most during the trip (~$5–8 USD)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at your favorite local restaurant from the trip — order your favorite Maldivian dish one last time (~$8–12 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Settle your guesthouse bill this evening to avoid a rushed checkout tomorrow morning. Confirm your ferry timing to the airport for the next day. Back up all your photos to cloud storage in case of any device issues during transit.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Maldives. Wake up, enjoy a last breakfast at the guesthouse, and take one final walk on the beach. Check out of your accommodation and arrange your ferry transfer to Velana International Airport. Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for the ferry ride and airport procedures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Velana International Airport. Complete check-in and security. Browse the duty-free shops for any last-minute gifts or Maldivian products. Reflect on 13 incredible days in paradise as you wait for your departure flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from the Maldives. Carry your memories, photos, and the warmth of your honeymoon with you as you head home.

meals.breakfast: Final guesthouse breakfast — make it special with your favorite items from the trip (~$5–7 USD)
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport café or terminal restaurant before departure (~$8–12 USD)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or at transit airport

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for the ferry to the airport — public ferries run on fixed schedules and missing one could mean missing your flight. Arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure. Keep all receipts for any duty-free purchases for customs declarations. Total estimated budget for the 13-day trip (excluding flights and accommodation): approximately $400–600 USD per couple for activities, meals, and transport.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00 at Velana International Airport (Malé)
day_by_day.afternoon: Airport arrival, immigration, and baggage collection. Transfer via speedboat or dhoni to your boutique stay in North Malé Atoll (approximately 20–45 minutes). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely self-guided stroll around the resort island to get your bearings — explore the beach, pool area, and house reef from the shore.
day_by_day.evening: Private Sunset Dhoni Cruise with Champagne — celebrate your arrival and the start of your honeymoon with a privately chartered traditional Maldivian dhoni sailing across the turquoise Indian Ocean. Watch the golden sunset over the horizon with champagne in hand.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight
meals.lunch: Light snack or meal at the airport arrival lounge or grab a bite at the resort's casual beachside café upon check-in
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the resort's main restaurant — try the catch-of-the-day grilled fish with coconut rice and local roshi bread. Budget-friendly set menu available.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm speedboat transfer times with your resort in advance. Keep swimwear accessible in carry-on for the dhoni cruise. The sunset cruise is best booked for around 17:30–18:30 in March.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and enjoy a sunrise walk along the beach. Head to the house reef for a relaxed introductory snorkel session directly from the resort — spot reef fish, sea turtles, and colorful corals just steps from the shore. Snorkel gear can be rented or borrowed from the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Coral Reef Snorkeling at Banana Reef — join a guided snorkeling excursion to Banana Reef, one of the Maldives' most iconic reefs in North Malé Atoll. Marvel at parrotfish, moray eels, Napoleon wrasse, and vibrant hard and soft corals. The boat ride takes approximately 30–45 minutes from your resort.
day_by_day.evening: Relax on the beach and watch the stars emerge. Enjoy a romantic beachside dinner under the open sky.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet breakfast at the resort — fresh tropical fruits, eggs made to order, local short eats like mas huni (tuna and coconut) with flatbread
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort's beach grill — grilled calamari, fresh salads, and coconut water
meals.dinner: Beachside à la carte dinner at the resort — grilled lobster or mahi-mahi with garlic butter, paired with a local mocktail or house wine

day_by_day.notes: Apply reef-safe sunscreen before snorkeling. Banana Reef is suitable for all skill levels. Book the guided excursion through the resort's activities desk the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a slow morning. Take a couples' yoga session on the beach or by the pool (often offered by boutique resorts at no extra charge). Afterward, lounge by the infinity pool and soak in the panoramic ocean views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Underwater Spa Treatment for Two — indulge in a deeply relaxing couples' massage or spa ritual in a semi-submerged treatment room surrounded by the ocean. Choose from traditional Maldivian healing techniques, aromatherapy, or a hot stone massage. Duration: approximately 60–90 minutes.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's overwater bar, followed by a romantic dinner for two.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast — order a tropical fruit platter, freshly squeezed juice, pastries, and coffee delivered to your villa
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — sandwiches, mezze platters, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Candlelit dinner at the resort's signature restaurant — try the Maldivian curry (mas riha) with steamed rice, papadum, and mango chutney. Mid-range tasting menu available.

day_by_day.notes: Book the underwater spa treatment at least 2 days in advance as slots fill quickly, especially for couples. Wear comfortable, loose clothing post-treatment.

day_by_day.morning: Morning snorkeling session at a nearby drift snorkel site arranged by the resort — drift gently with the current through a channel teeming with marine life including sharks, rays, and schools of fish. Guided by a resort marine biologist.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the local inhabited island nearest to your resort (accessible by a short dhoni ride). Explore the narrow streets, visit the local mosque, browse small shops for handmade souvenirs like lacquerware and woven mats, and interact with friendly locals.
day_by_day.evening: Private Sandbank Picnic Dinner — be whisked away by speedboat to a secluded, uninhabited sandbank in the middle of the ocean. A personal chef and butler set up a romantic candlelit dinner under the stars on the pristine white sand surrounded by nothing but the Indian Ocean.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast — fresh juices, tropical fruits, local tuna curry, eggs, and pastries
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local teashop on the inhabited island — try short eats like bajiya (fish pastry), gulha (fish balls), and sweet black tea. Very affordable and authentic.
meals.dinner: Fully included in the Private Sandbank Picnic Dinner experience — multi-course private chef menu featuring fresh seafood, salads, dessert, and beverages

day_by_day.notes: The sandbank dinner is weather-dependent — have a backup indoor romantic dinner option ready. Bring insect repellent for the sandbank. The local island visit is free but bring small cash for souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Maldivian Cooking Class and Local Market Visit — start with an early morning trip to a local fish and produce market with a local chef guide. Learn about Maldivian ingredients like smoked tuna (rihaakuru), breadfruit, and coconut. Return to the resort kitchen for a hands-on cooking class making traditional dishes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Free afternoon — relax on the beach with a good book, enjoy water sports offered by the resort (kayaking, paddleboarding, or windsurfing at additional cost), or simply float in the calm lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the fruits of your morning labor — dine on the dishes you prepared in the cooking class, served in a special setting arranged by the resort chef.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the market visit — fresh fruit, yogurt, and coffee at the resort café
meals.lunch: Lunch is part of the cooking class experience — taste all the dishes you prepared including mas huni, garudhiya (tuna broth soup), and coconut flatbread
meals.dinner: Your own cooked Maldivian feast from the morning class, served at a special table — supplement with a bottle of wine or mocktails from the resort bar

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class is a wonderful cultural experience and a unique honeymoon memory. Wear closed-toe shoes for the fish market visit. Book the class 2–3 days in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning of leisure — sleep in, enjoy breakfast in bed, and spend time in your villa. If your boutique stay has an overwater bungalow or water villa option, this is a perfect day to upgrade or enjoy the in-villa plunge pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided dolphin watching cruise — North Malé Atoll is famous for its large spinner dolphin pods. Join a resort-organized afternoon boat trip to spot dolphins leaping and playing in the wake of the boat.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the beach followed by a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast — fresh tropical fruits, eggs benedict, croissants, and freshly brewed coffee
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at the resort beach bar — fish tacos, grilled corn, and fresh coconut
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's overwater or beachside restaurant — grilled barracuda or snapper with sautéed vegetables and a shared dessert platter

day_by_day.notes: Dolphin sightings are common in North Malé Atoll but not guaranteed — the boat trip itself is scenic and enjoyable regardless. Bring a camera with a zoom lens.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning sunrise snorkel at the house reef — the early hours offer the calmest waters and best visibility. Look for sleeping nurse sharks, sea turtles feeding on coral, and octopuses emerging from crevices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Day trip to Malé city — take the resort's scheduled speedboat transfer to the capital. Visit the Grand Friday Mosque (Masjid Al-Sultan Muhammad Thakurufaanu Al Auzam), the National Museum, the colorful fish market, and the vibrant local streets. A fascinating contrast to the tranquil resort life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by early evening. Enjoy a quiet night in — order room service and watch the stars from your villa terrace or beach.

meals.breakfast: Quick resort breakfast before departing for Malé — fruit, toast, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch in Malé at a local restaurant — try a traditional rice and curry meal (garudhiya with rice, pickle, and chili) at a local eatery. Very affordable.
meals.dinner: Room service dinner at the villa — select from the resort's in-room dining menu. Treat yourselves to a decadent dessert to end the week.

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly when visiting Malé — cover shoulders and knees, especially near mosques. The National Museum has a small entrance fee. Keep valuables secure in the city.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning — sleep in after the busy day in Malé. Enjoy a long breakfast and a slow start. Take a gentle swim in the lagoon or lounge in a hammock strung between palm trees.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling at a second reef site — ask the resort's dive center to recommend a different snorkeling spot from Banana Reef. Options in North Malé Atoll include Kuda Haa, Okobe Thila, or HP Reef for more advanced underwater scenery including overhangs, caves, and large pelagic fish.
day_by_day.evening: Couples' sundowner on the beach — bring a bottle of wine or champagne and watch the sunset together from a private spot on the beach. Many boutique resorts can arrange a private beach setup with cushions, lanterns, and a fruit platter.

meals.breakfast: Full resort buffet — take your time and try everything, including the Maldivian breakfast station with mas huni and roshi
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort pool bar — bruschetta, fresh salads, and tropical smoothies
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's main restaurant — try a themed night if available (seafood night, BBQ night, or international cuisine night common at boutique resorts)

day_by_day.notes: HP Reef (also known as Hans Hass Place) is a protected marine area and one of the best snorkel/dive sites in the Maldives — highly recommended if accessible from your resort.

day_by_day.morning: Morning spa session — return to the resort spa for individual treatments. Try a traditional Maldivian body scrub using coconut, sea salt, and local herbs, followed by a refreshing dip in the ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding adventure — explore the lagoon and surrounding sandbanks by kayak or SUP. Many boutique resorts in North Malé Atoll have calm, shallow lagoons perfect for self-guided paddling. Spot reef fish through the crystal-clear water from above.
day_by_day.evening: Second Private Sunset Dhoni Cruise — if you loved the first one, consider booking a second sunset cruise, this time with a small private dinner served on board the dhoni as the sun dips below the horizon.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast — smoothie bowls, avocado toast, and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch from the resort to enjoy on the water while kayaking — sandwiches, fruit, and cold drinks
meals.dinner: On-board dhoni dinner (if booked) or resort restaurant — fresh grilled seafood platter for two with sides and dessert

day_by_day.notes: Apply waterproof sunscreen generously before kayaking — the midday sun in March can be intense. Stay hydrated throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning — completely unstructured time to do whatever feels right. Sleep in, read, swim, or simply sit on the beach and breathe. This is your honeymoon — embrace the slow pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Introductory scuba diving experience (Discover Scuba) — even if you've never dived before, most resorts offer a beginner pool session followed by a shallow open-water dive with a certified instructor. Experience the underwater world from a whole new perspective.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory romantic dinner — dress up and enjoy the most special dinner of the trip at the resort's finest dining venue or arrange a private beach dinner with the resort team.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort buffet breakfast — no rush today
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the beach bar before the afternoon dive — keep it simple with a sandwich and fresh juice
meals.dinner: Special romantic dinner — choose the resort's premium dining experience. Opt for a seafood tasting menu or a private overwater table if available. Splurge slightly for this memorable evening.

day_by_day.notes: For the Discover Scuba experience, inform the instructor of any medical conditions in advance. Do not fly within 12–18 hours after diving. The romantic dinner can be arranged through the resort's concierge with advance notice.

day_by_day.morning: Final snorkeling adventure — make the most of the underwater world with one last guided snorkeling excursion. Ask the resort's marine biologist for a personalized site recommendation based on conditions and your experience over the past days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir shopping and resort exploration — browse the resort's boutique for local crafts, Maldivian jewelry, and keepsakes. Spend time photographing the island, the lagoon, and each other for lasting honeymoon memories. Visit the resort's marine biology station if available to learn about coral restoration efforts.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell cocktails and a reflective evening stroll along the beach under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Full resort buffet — enjoy every bite knowing the trip is winding down
meals.lunch: Casual beachside lunch — grilled fish skewers, fresh coconut, and tropical fruit salad
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort with a focus on Maldivian cuisine — order traditional dishes you haven't tried yet, such as bis keemiya (stuffed pastry) or fihunu mas (grilled reef fish) with local sides

day_by_day.notes: Check the resort's boutique for authentic locally made products — avoid mass-produced items. Coral and shells are protected and cannot be taken from the Maldives.

day_by_day.morning: Last sunrise swim and final house reef snorkel — wake before dawn to catch the magical Maldivian sunrise over the ocean. Take one final swim in the warm Indian Ocean and say goodbye to the house reef.
day_by_day.afternoon: Checkout procedures and luggage preparation. Spend the remaining time relaxing by the pool or on the beach. Most resorts allow late checkout or luggage storage if your transfer is in the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the resort — a final celebration of your honeymoon. Share your favorite moments from the trip over a leisurely meal.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — indulge in your favorite dishes from the past 12 days
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the pool bar — keep it simple for travel preparation
meals.dinner: Final dinner at the resort's main restaurant — order your favorite dish from the trip as a farewell. Toast to your honeymoon with a glass of champagne.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure transfer time with the resort. Settle any outstanding bills the night before to avoid a rushed checkout. Back up all photos to the cloud.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in paradise — enjoy a last breakfast at the resort. Take a slow walk on the beach, collect a handful of sand as a memory, and breathe in the salt air one last time. Complete checkout and prepare for the speedboat transfer to Velana International Airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Speedboat transfer to Malé (20–45 minutes). Arrive at Velana International Airport with ample time for check-in, security, and immigration. Browse duty-free shops for last-minute gifts — Maldivian honey, local spices, or resort-branded items make great souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from the Maldives — carry the memories of an unforgettable honeymoon home with you.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — tropical fruits, local short eats, and freshly brewed coffee
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or café at Velana International Airport — light meal before boarding
meals.dinner: In-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure. Maldivian Rufiyaa can be exchanged back at the airport. Ensure all dive logs and resort receipts are packed safely. Wishing you a wonderful honeymoon filled with love and lasting memories!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Maldives Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: North Malé Atoll, Maldives Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Private Sunset Dhoni Cruise with Champagne
experiences.description: Sail across the turquoise Indian Ocean on a traditional Maldivian dhoni boat, privately chartered for two. Watch the sun melt into the horizon while sipping champagne and enjoying a curated platter of local and international delicacies. A quintessential romantic experience perfect for honeymooners.

experiences.name: Coral Reef Snorkeling at Banana Reef
experiences.description: Explore one of the Maldives' most iconic and vibrant coral reefs, teeming with parrotfish, moray eels, sea turtles, and colorful reef sharks. Guided snorkeling tours provide equipment and expert narration, making this an unforgettable underwater adventure for couples and luxury travelers alike.

experiences.name: Underwater Spa Treatment for Two
experiences.description: Indulge in a couples' massage or spa ritual in a semi-submerged treatment room surrounded by the ocean. Many luxury resorts offer glass-floor or open-air overwater spa pavilions where you can hear the waves and watch marine life while being pampered with traditional Maldivian coconut and frangipani treatments.

experiences.name: Private Sandbank Picnic Dinner
experiences.description: Be whisked away by speedboat to a secluded, uninhabited sandbank in the middle of the ocean. A personal butler sets up a candlelit dinner table on the white sand, complete with fresh Maldivian seafood, tropical fruits, and fine wine under a canopy of stars — the ultimate honeymoon dining experience.

experiences.name: Maldivian Cooking Class and Local Market Visit
experiences.description: Discover the rich culinary heritage of the Maldives with a hands-on cooking class led by a local chef. Begin with a guided tour of the Malé local market to source fresh tuna, coconut, and tropical spices, then learn to prepare traditional dishes like Mas Huni (tuna and coconut salad) and Garudhiya (fish broth). A culturally immersive and delicious experience.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrival at Velana International Airport at 13:00. Met by a private resort representative for a seamless VIP transfer via luxury speedboat to your boutique resort in North Malé Atoll (approx. 20–45 min). Check in, receive a welcome drink of fresh coconut water and champagne, and settle into your overwater or beach villa. Take a leisurely stroll along the resort's private beach and familiarize yourself with the property.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a romantic welcome dinner at the resort's signature overwater restaurant. Watch the sun dip below the Indian Ocean horizon from your table as you savor a curated tasting menu of fresh Maldivian seafood — grilled lobster, seared tuna tataki, and coconut panna cotta — paired with a bottle of chilled Blanc de Blancs champagne.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight)
meals.lunch: Light welcome bites and tropical fruit platter served upon arrival at the resort
meals.dinner: Private welcome dinner at the resort's signature overwater restaurant — multi-course tasting menu with champagne pairing

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — keep the schedule relaxed and stress-free. Confirm all upcoming experience bookings with the resort concierge upon check-in. Request pillow menu, villa preferences, and any special honeymoon amenities (rose petals, in-villa champagne setup).

day_by_day.morning: Begin your first full day with a lavish in-villa breakfast delivered by private butler — freshly baked pastries, tropical fruit platters, eggs cooked to order, and freshly pressed juices served on your overwater deck. Afterward, take a guided house reef snorkeling session with the resort's marine biologist, exploring the colorful coral gardens and spotting reef sharks, turtles, and vibrant reef fish right off your villa's steps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in the 'Underwater Spa Treatment for Two' — a signature couples' massage in the resort's semi-submerged treatment room, surrounded by the mesmerizing blue ocean. Post-treatment, unwind in the spa's relaxation pool with herbal teas and fresh fruit.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's over-lagoon bar, sipping on handcrafted passion fruit mojitos and local Maldivian-inspired cocktails. Dinner at the resort's beachside grill restaurant — whole grilled snapper, prawn skewers, and handmade flatbreads, with toes in the sand and a live acoustic guitarist serenading you.

meals.breakfast: Lavish in-villa butler breakfast on the overwater deck
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — fresh ceviche, lobster rolls, and chilled coconut water at the resort's pool bar
meals.dinner: Beachside grill dinner with live acoustic music — fresh catch of the day, grilled prawns, and artisan desserts

day_by_day.notes: Book the Underwater Spa Treatment well in advance as slots are limited. Ask the marine biologist about the best time to spot turtles on the house reef — typically early morning.

day_by_day.morning: Set out on the 'Coral Reef Snorkeling at Banana Reef' excursion — one of the Maldives' most iconic dive sites, located in North Malé Atoll. A private boat transfers you to this protected reef where you'll snorkel among parrotfish, moray eels, Napoleon wrasse, and dense coral formations. A professional guide accompanies you to enhance the experience and ensure safety.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a leisurely afternoon. Lounge by the infinity pool with a cocktail in hand, or explore the resort's water sports center — try stand-up paddleboarding or kayaking across the crystal-clear lagoon at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Board a traditionally decorated Maldivian dhoni for the 'Private Sunset Dhoni Cruise with Champagne.' Sail across the turquoise Indian Ocean as the sky turns shades of gold and crimson, sipping on chilled Moët & Chandon champagne with canapés — smoked salmon blinis, truffle crostini, and fresh oysters — while your private crew navigates the serene waters.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast at the main dining pavilion — live egg station, fresh pastries, tropical fruits, and Maldivian fish curry
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet picnic lunch on the boat during the Banana Reef excursion — sandwiches, fresh fruit, and chilled juices
meals.dinner: Dinner on the dhoni cruise followed by a late-night à la carte dining at the resort's fine-dining restaurant — lobster bisque, wagyu beef tenderloin, and chocolate fondant

day_by_day.notes: Banana Reef is a protected marine area — use reef-safe sunscreen only. The dhoni cruise typically departs 1 hour before sunset; confirm exact timing with the concierge based on sunset time for March 17.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a slow, romantic morning. Sleep in and savor a champagne breakfast in bed arranged by your butler — fresh croissants, smoked salmon, scrambled eggs with truffle, and a bottle of rosé champagne. Spend the late morning reading and relaxing on your private villa deck, dipping into your plunge pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a 'Maldivian Cooking Class and Local Market Visit' — your private chef guide takes you on a speedboat to a nearby local island to browse the vibrant morning market, selecting fresh tuna, tropical spices, and coconut. Return to the resort's culinary studio to learn how to prepare traditional Maldivian dishes: mas riha (fish curry), bis keemiya (stuffed pastries), and saagu bondibai (sago pudding).
day_by_day.evening: Dine on the dishes you prepared together in a private candlelit setting on the beach — a truly personal and memorable culinary experience. Finish the evening with a stargazing session arranged by the resort, lying on deck chairs on the sandbank beside the resort with a telescope and a knowledgeable guide pointing out constellations over the Indian Ocean.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast in bed — butler service with rosé champagne, croissants, smoked salmon, and truffle eggs
meals.lunch: Snacks and fresh juices at the local island market during the cooking class excursion
meals.dinner: Candlelit private beach dinner featuring dishes you cooked yourself during the cooking class, with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class is a wonderful cultural experience — request a vegetarian or dietary-adjusted version if needed. Confirm stargazing availability with the resort; March skies in the Maldives are typically clear and ideal for stargazing.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise yoga session on the overwater yoga pavilion, guided by the resort's private yoga instructor. The session is tailored for two, set against the breathtaking backdrop of the Indian Ocean awakening in golden light. Follow with a healthy smoothie bowl breakfast at the wellness café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon on a private snorkeling expedition to a nearby coral garden selected by the resort's marine team — different from Banana Reef, offering a chance to spot manta rays (seasonally present in March) and schools of colorful reef fish. Your private guide accompanies you on a resort speedboat.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the 'Private Sandbank Picnic Dinner' — be whisked away by speedboat to a secluded, uninhabited sandbank in the middle of the Indian Ocean. A personal chef has set up an elegant table with lanterns, white linen, and fresh flowers. Dine on a bespoke menu of fresh seafood, Maldivian-inspired dishes, and decadent desserts under a canopy of stars, with the sound of gentle waves as your only backdrop.

meals.breakfast: Post-yoga wellness breakfast at the resort's health café — acai bowls, green smoothies, avocado toast, and fresh coconut water
meals.lunch: Poolside light lunch — sushi platter, fresh salads, and chilled sparkling water with citrus
meals.dinner: Private sandbank picnic dinner — bespoke multi-course menu by a personal chef with wine and champagne pairing

day_by_day.notes: The Private Sandbank Picnic Dinner is the crown jewel of romantic experiences — confirm booking at least 48 hours in advance and communicate any dietary preferences or special requests (e.g., a honeymoon cake or personalized message in the sand).

day_by_day.morning: A restful free morning to enjoy your villa and resort facilities at leisure. Take a morning swim in the lagoon, enjoy a slow breakfast on your deck, and perhaps visit the resort's boutique to browse locally crafted jewelry and souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on a dolphin-watching cruise in the waters around North Malé Atoll — spinner dolphins are frequently spotted in these waters in the late afternoon. The resort arranges a private boat with snacks and beverages. If dolphins are spotted, you may have the opportunity to snorkel alongside them.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a romantic in-villa dinner prepared and served by your private butler and chef. A specially curated menu is set up on your overwater deck — chilled oysters, butter-poached lobster tail, saffron risotto, and a decadent chocolate and raspberry tart, with candles and rose petals adorning the setting.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely in-villa breakfast on the deck — fresh pastries, tropical fruit, yogurt parfait, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Snacks and drinks on the dolphin-watching cruise — cheese and charcuterie board, fresh fruit, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Private in-villa romantic dinner on the overwater deck — butler-served multi-course menu with champagne and candle setting

day_by_day.notes: Dolphin sightings are common but not guaranteed. The resort's marine team selects the best location based on recent sightings. Inform the butler in advance about the in-villa dinner setup so they can prepare the decorations.

day_by_day.morning: Midpoint of the trip — celebrate with a special morning. Arrange for a private sunrise breakfast on the resort's jetty, with a table set over the water, watching the sun rise over the Indian Ocean. Afterward, take a guided kayaking tour of the mangrove lagoon on the island's edge — a peaceful, nature-rich experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the spa for individual treatments — choose from a Maldivian coconut oil body wrap, a deep tissue massage, or a hydrating facial. Spend the remainder of the afternoon floating in the overwater hammock net attached to your villa or lounging on the private beach.
day_by_day.evening: Join the resort's weekly cultural evening — a Bodu Beru (traditional Maldivian drumming and dance) performance on the beach, with a festive buffet dinner featuring the best of Maldivian cuisine: tuna curry, roshi (flatbread), hedhikaa (local snacks), and fresh grilled seafood.

meals.breakfast: Private sunrise breakfast on the resort jetty — continental spread with pastries, fresh fruits, eggs, and champagne
meals.lunch: Light spa lunch at the wellness café — grain bowls, fresh juices, and herbal teas
meals.dinner: Bodu Beru cultural evening buffet dinner on the beach — Maldivian traditional cuisine with local desserts and mocktails

day_by_day.notes: The Bodu Beru performance is a wonderful cultural immersion experience — participate in the drumming if invited! Confirm the cultural evening schedule with the resort as it may vary by week.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning snorkeling session at a different reef location recommended by the resort's dive center — perhaps a drift snorkel along a channel known for strong currents that bring in pelagic fish. Accompanied by a certified guide for safety and maximum enjoyment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend a relaxing afternoon at the resort's infinity pool, enjoying curated cocktails from the pool butler. Alternatively, book a private sailing lesson on a catamaran in the resort's lagoon — a fun and active way to connect with the ocean.
day_by_day.evening: Second 'Private Sunset Dhoni Cruise with Champagne' — this time, request a different route through the North Malé Atoll, sailing past uninhabited sandbanks and watching the sunset from a new vantage point. Return to the resort for a late dinner at the resort's Asian fusion restaurant — fresh tuna sashimi, prawn tempura, miso-glazed black cod, and green tea mochi.

meals.breakfast: Resort main restaurant breakfast — full à la carte with Maldivian fish curry, fresh juices, and specialty teas
meals.lunch: Poolside lunch — lobster tacos, fresh ceviche, and tropical fruit sorbet
meals.dinner: Asian fusion restaurant dinner — sashimi, black cod, and artisan desserts with sake or Japanese whisky pairing

day_by_day.notes: If you enjoyed Banana Reef snorkeling, ask the dive center about snorkeling at Manta Point or Kuda Haa — both accessible from North Malé Atoll and excellent for March conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Take a full morning off for pure relaxation — sleep in, enjoy a butler breakfast on your deck, and spend time in your private plunge pool. Read, journal, or simply watch the fish swimming beneath your overwater villa. This is your day to recharge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby local Maldivian island with your private guide for a cultural immersion tour — walk through the local village, visit the Friday mosque, watch local craftsmen weave traditional mats (thundu kunaa), and shop for handmade souvenirs. A truly authentic glimpse into Maldivian island life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a romantic evening. Arrange for a private beach bonfire with the resort's team — sit beside a crackling fire on the sand, roasting marshmallows and sipping on aged rum cocktails, with the Milky Way stretching above you. Light dinner of gourmet charcuterie, artisan cheeses, and fresh bread served beside the bonfire.

meals.breakfast: Slow in-villa breakfast — fresh fruit, yogurt, pastries, and specialty coffee served by your butler
meals.lunch: Fresh coconut and local snacks on the local island visit; light lunch at a local café if available
meals.dinner: Private beach bonfire dinner — gourmet charcuterie and cheese board, fresh bread, and rum cocktails

day_by_day.notes: The local island visit is a respectful cultural experience — dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered) when visiting the village and mosque. Purchase locally made crafts to support the community.

day_by_day.morning: Morning snorkeling at the house reef — by now you'll be familiar with the layout and can explore independently or with a guide to revisit favorite spots. Look out for octopus, nudibranch, and juvenile reef sharks in the shallower sections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Couples' spa afternoon — book back-to-back treatments: begin with a traditional Maldivian Dhivehi herbal steam ritual, followed by a four-hand massage (two therapists working simultaneously) for the ultimate indulgence. End with a private Jacuzzi soak in the spa's ocean-view terrace.
day_by_day.evening: Chef's table experience — a private, interactive dinner hosted by the resort's executive chef. Seated at a special table in or adjacent to the kitchen, you'll enjoy a personalized tasting menu of 7–9 courses, with the chef explaining each dish and its inspiration. Wine pairing curated by the resort's sommelier.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast — wide spread of international and Maldivian dishes, live cooking stations
meals.lunch: Spa cuisine lunch — light, nourishing dishes such as quinoa salad, grilled fish, and fresh juices served in the spa lounge
meals.dinner: Chef's table private tasting menu — 7–9 courses with wine pairing, hosted by the executive chef

day_by_day.notes: The Chef's Table is one of the most exclusive dining experiences at luxury Maldivian resorts — book it well in advance. Communicate any dietary restrictions or preferences so the menu can be fully personalized.

day_by_day.morning: Join a guided stand-up paddleboard yoga session on the lagoon at sunrise — a unique and playful wellness experience that combines balance, mindfulness, and the beauty of the ocean. Followed by a healthy breakfast at the resort's wellness café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final snorkeling adventure — the resort's marine team arranges a special 'snorkel safari' visiting three different reef spots in one afternoon by private boat, maximizing your underwater exploration before the trip ends. Spot turtles, rays, and schools of fusiliers in their natural habitat.
day_by_day.evening: Romantic anniversary/honeymoon dinner on the resort's private overwater platform — a table for two set above the ocean, decorated with floating candles, tropical flowers, and fairy lights. A bespoke menu is crafted by the chef: Champagne and oysters to start, followed by butter-poached lobster, wagyu beef, and a custom honeymoon cake with a personalized message. Live violin serenade as you dine.

meals.breakfast: Post-yoga wellness breakfast at the health café — smoothie bowls, avocado toast, and cold-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Light lunch on the snorkel safari boat — gourmet sandwiches, fresh fruit, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Special overwater romantic dinner — bespoke honeymoon menu with champagne, live violin, and custom honeymoon cake

day_by_day.notes: This is the penultimate evening — make it the most special night of the trip. Arrange for the resort to set up the overwater platform with personalized touches (initials in flowers, a framed photo from the trip, etc.). Communicate all special requests at least 48 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final full morning — wake up early for one last sunrise over the Indian Ocean from your villa deck. Take a slow, reflective swim in the lagoon. Your butler prepares a farewell in-villa breakfast with all your favorites from the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at leisure — final poolside lounging, last-minute spa treatments, or a gentle kayak around the lagoon. Visit the resort boutique for any remaining souvenirs or gifts. Begin light packing in preparation for departure the following day.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the resort's main fine-dining restaurant — a celebratory meal to mark the end of your honeymoon journey. Choose freely from the à la carte menu, savoring your favorite dishes from the trip. The resort may prepare a farewell surprise — a small dessert platter or personalized card from the team.

meals.breakfast: Final in-villa butler breakfast — personalized selection of your favorite items from the trip
meals.lunch: Casual poolside lunch — light bites, fresh juices, and tropical cocktails
meals.dinner: Farewell à la carte dinner at the resort's fine-dining restaurant — celebrate the end of your honeymoon with your favorite dishes and a bottle of vintage champagne

day_by_day.notes: Request a late checkout for Day 13 if your flight allows. Settle any outstanding bills and confirm departure transfer arrangements with the concierge. Leave a gratuity for your butler and key staff who made the trip exceptional.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy one last breakfast on your villa deck, taking in the view of the turquoise lagoon you've called home for 13 days. Take a final dip in the ocean or plunge pool. Pack remaining belongings and prepare for checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the resort with a heartfelt farewell from the team. Board your private speedboat transfer back to Velana International Airport, carrying memories of an extraordinary honeymoon in paradise. Arrive at the airport with ample time for your departure flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Velana International Airport. Reflect on the magical journey — the sunsets, the underwater world, the flavors, and the romance of the Maldives.

meals.breakfast: Final in-villa or resort breakfast — continental spread with fresh pastries, tropical fruits, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Airport lounge lunch or light snacks at the Velana International Airport premium lounge
meals.dinner: In-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Confirm flight details and transfer timing the evening before. The speedboat transfer to the airport typically takes 20–45 minutes — allow sufficient buffer time. Keep all travel documents, resort receipts, and special mementos (menus, photos, etc.) safely stored for cherished memories of your honeymoon.
